note: [agent-bulk] shw 9012 (102.7 MeV, 2 seg, nuecc): correct, and the two-piece membership is the physics, not a merge error. The reco start is EXACTLY the nu vertex, and what the pictures show at az-055, az+085 and el+60 is: a 9.7 cm narrow stem leaving the vertex, then about 20 cm of empty space with no charge at all, then a dense 10.3 cm blob (segment 50010, cluster 50) at 32.3 cm / 13.7 deg, taken by pass3_cone. That is the textbook 100 MeV electron in LAr -- MIP stem for less than one radiation length, a hard bremsstrahlung, the photon crossing roughly one conversion length (9/7 X0, about 18 cm in LAr, against the ~20 cm gap measured off the frames) invisibly, then pair-producing into the blob. The transverse offset implied by 13.7 deg at 32.3 cm is 7.6 cm, inside a Moliere radius. So the gap is an argument FOR the merge, not against it, and I looked for the alternative (a detached pi0 photon swallowed by pass3_cone) and could not make it fit a nuecc event whose shower starts on the vertex. Nothing is missing either: the acceptance plot has TWO orange squares and ZERO blue circles out to 42 cm, and every non-member is behind or sideways -- 41009 at 13.0 cm / 165.5 deg, 40008 at 19.5 cm / 116.7 deg, 39007 at 29.3 cm / 121.8 deg, 19006 at 122.7 cm. Segment 9011 (4.1 cm, its own sub-20 MeV shower, same cluster 9) shares the vertex point so the table reports it as dist 0 / angle 0, but in every frame it leaves the star in a clearly different direction from the stem -- the second prong of the interaction, correctly not absorbed. No pi0 group and no candidate: there is no second EM object above 20 MeV anywhere in this event, so this is a single-shower topology, not a pairing failure. Showers NOT looked at: the 5 the scope rule skipped (9011 and four others), all below 20 MeV. Clustering statement, silent on PID.
